newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds, dollar rise before expected Fed rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds, dollar rise before expected Fed rate hike.

text.p: Stocks, bonds and the dollar rose Tuesday, as the prospect of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve at its policy-making meeting failed to dampen Wall Street's bullish mood.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 8.69 points at 6,913.94.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a 13-9 margin on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 251 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 6.65 points at 1,249.29.
Analysts said a quarter-point increase already was priced into the market, and they believed that Monday's 100-point leap in the Dow index was the equivelent of a relief rally.
"We are getting a relief rally before the Fed tightening," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyons & Ross.
"There might not be any reaction if the Fed tightens by 25 basis points as we have already had one. But if it does not tighten, the market may be very disappointed for a few hours," Blumberg said.

The central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee started its meeting at 9 a.m. EST (1400 GMT) Tuesday and following recent practice, the decision should be known around 2:15 p.m. (1915 GMT).

Recent comments by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan appear to have conditioned financial markets to expect a token rise in interest rates as the central bank aims to sustain moderate economic growth and head off potential inflationary pressures that could emerge by late this year or early next year.
A larger rate increase, however, might trigger a sell-off while a decision not to tighten could prompt a rally, analysts said.

"The message of the stock market today is that the Fed will not only raise rates, but its strategy will work in the sense that we will see the economy slow. In time, though, not right away," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
The bond market, however, was boosted by rumours -- later discounted -- that the Fed would not raise rates at the FOMC meeting which ends Wednesday.
In the bond market, the key 30-year Treasury bond rose a quarter point, reducing its yield to 6.90 percent from 6.92 percent at Monday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The dollar rose as higher interest rates would make yields on U.S. investments more attractive.

"It's an interest rate play," said Elliott Dix, an assistant vice president at Signet Bank, referring to one of the reasons behind the dollar's gains. "Rates in the United States are expected to go up. Rates in Switzerland and Germany are expected to stay where they are or (move) lower."
The dollar rose to 1.6924 German marks and 123.91 Japanese yen from 1.6880 marks and 122.85 yen late Monday.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 blue chip share index finished 55.9 points higher at 4,270.7, just below the day's best levels. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average finished 395.79 points, or 2.19 percent, higher at 18,439.61.
